clue.text: Conveyance by river line provides many ups and downs

parts.note: a tram is a conveyance for passengers in a city street
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tram running along the river line is a bumpy ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of what the thing does rather than a synonym: you bounce up and down on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast's sprung canvas sheet throws the user up and lets them fall again, over and over.

clue.text: Proceed in a body, right round in top

indicators.note: the right-and-round letters are placed in the word for the top

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An instruction to march as a group, wheeling right round at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To move together as a crowd or a company of soldiers, filing along in a mass.

clue.text: Jack in a role follows a way to scale the starry heights

indicators.note: the jack-in-role part comes after the 'a way' part in the answer

parts.note: taken as written
ST is short for street, a way

indicators.note: the sailor's letters go in the word for a role

parts.note: taken as written
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, abbreviated AB for able seaman

explanation.surface: An actor playing a sailor follows a path up to the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor here, not a playing card or a lifting tool; 'follows' puts the sailor-in-role part after the 'a way' part.
explanation.definitionFit: The old instrument measured the altitude of stars above the horizon, used for navigation and astronomy.

clue.text: Sharp reminders that a member's been asleep

definitions.text: Sharp reminders that a member's been asleep

parts.words: Sharp reminders that a member's been asleep
parts.note: a limb (member) that has gone numb tingles with prickling sensations as it wakes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' reads as someone in a club dozing, but it is an arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickling tingling felt when blood returns to a limb that has gone numb.

clue.text: With a nautical inclination to sling it

annotationWithheld.why: With a nautical inclination to sling it (7): the anagram fodder 'sling it' has no separate indicator; 'sling' would have to be both fodder and the anagram signal
annotationWithheld.clue: With a nautical inclination to sling it

clue.text: No bird over fifty is so called

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird sits over, above, the fifty

parts.note: taken as written
a mina (myna) is an Asian starling known for mimicking speech
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An ageing bird over fifty can no longer be called one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists in name only: it is so termed but not really.

clue.text: King-saint of the French interior

indicators.note: the French article is put in the interior of the word of

parts.note: taken as written
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A royal saint from deep inside France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interior' looks like part of 'the French interior' (inland France), but it signals the French article going inside the clue's 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: St Olaf was the Norwegian king who Christianised his country and became its patron saint.

clue.text: It's bad in the French city

indicators.note: the bad letters sit in the French article

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A complaint that conditions are poor in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French city' reads as one phrase, but 'the French' gives LE and only 'city' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large industrial city in northern France.

clue.text: A noted poem of the North country

definitions.text: A noted poem of the North country

parts.words: A noted poem of the North country
parts.note: a tone poem, set to musical notes, named in Latin after a Nordic land; Sibelius wrote it

explanation.walkthrough: 'noted' means both famous and written in musical notes: this is Sibelius's patriotic tone poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius's 1899 symphonic poem carries the Latin name of his Nordic homeland.

clue.text: Piglet, he accepts a challenge and has to take punishment

parts.note: a runt is the smallest piglet of a litter
taken as written
throwing down a gauntlet, a glove, was a challenge to fight

explanation.surface: A little pig takes up a challenge and must suffer the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a soldier made to pass between two lines of men who struck him; now to face severe criticism.

clue.text: Dismissed' in general service excursions

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
taken as written
GS is the abbreviation for general service

explanation.surface: Soldiers sent away on general-service trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Outings are pleasure trips, days out away from home.

clue.text: Sounds like a college crying into its beer

indicators.note: the answer is what the college's name sounds like when spoken

parts.note: Magdalen College, Oxford

explanation.surface: A drunken college reduced to tearful self-pity.
explanation.walkthrough: Magdalen College at Oxford (and Magdalene at Cambridge) are pronounced like the answer, from Mary Magdalene, often painted weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully sentimental, the way a drunk weeps over a pint.

clue.text: Post-trial trial

definitions.meaning: the supervised release a convicted offender serves after the court case instead of prison
a testing period for a new employee or member

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the court's non-custodial sentence after conviction and a period of testing someone's suitability.

clue.text: In Greek this is out

parts.note: a Greek letter, first of thanatos (death), was marked against the names of the dead or condemned

explanation.walkthrough: Ancient Greek jurors and record-keepers marked the dead or condemned with this letter, the initial of thanatos, death: they were out.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth Greek letter, used as a mark of death in antiquity.

clue.text: Poet made sound supplication in the street

indicators.note: the poet's surname is how the word for a plea sounds when spoken aloud by folk in the street, which also names a London street

parts.note: to make an earnest plea to God is to pray, so this is prayed

explanation.surface: A poet praying out loud on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: W.M. Praed was a Regency comic poet; Praed Street, by Paddington station in London, is named after his family.
explanation.definitionFit: Winthrop Mackworth Praed wrote light verse in the 1820s and 1830s.

clue.text: "A winning wave … In the tempestuous ___ " (Herrick)

parts.note: a line from Herrick's Delight in Disorder, about a woman's underskirt swirling as she moves

explanation.walkthrough: Herrick's 'Delight in Disorder' praises 'A winning wave, deserving note, / In the tempestuous petticoat'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the underskirt worn beneath a dress, in Herrick's poem.

clue.text: Flower felt by the unspoilt child of a Phrygian king ?

definitions.text: Flower felt by the unspoilt child of a Phrygian king ?

parts.words: Flower felt by the unspoilt child of a Phrygian king
parts.note: a yellow flower; King Midas turned all he touched to gold, so the cane on his child would be gilded, and a child not spoilt has not been spared it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare the rod and spoil the child': an unspoilt child has felt the rod, and Midas of Phrygia turned all he touched to gold, so his child's rod would be golden.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall plant with plumes of yellow flowers, named for its colour and stem.

clue.text: They're ready for a summer

parts.note: a summer is one who sums, and a ready table of calculations helps them

explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is the season in the surface, but here it is someone who does sums; ready reckoners are printed tables of calculations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready reckoners are books of pre-worked calculations, ready to help anyone adding up.

clue.text: And so three triangular points appear in proof

definitions.text: And so three triangular points appear in proof

parts.words: And so three triangular points appear in proof
parts.note: the mathematician's symbol of three dots arranged in a triangle, meaning 'and so', used in proofs

explanation.walkthrough: In geometry proofs the symbol ∴, three dots in a triangle, stands for this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'consequently', and its symbol of three dots is used in logic and maths proofs.

clue.text: Was against Work, having struck an attitude

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to strike an attitude is to adopt a pose, so this is posed

explanation.surface: Someone resisted the job and stood there in a defiant stance.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opposed something is to have resisted or disagreed with it.

clue.text: Issue of an aquatic mammal tail to head

indicators.note: the final letter of the mammal's name is moved round to the front

parts.note: the manatee or sea cow is a large aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: Something comes out of a sea creature from back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail to head' moves the last E of MANATEE to the start, giving E + MANATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or proceed from a source.

clue.text: Capital association of RAF and Gunner types

parts.note: AC, aircraftman, is the lowest rank in the Royal Air Force
CRA, Commander Royal Artillery, is the senior Gunner officer of a division

explanation.surface: A capital city formed by an alliance of airmen and artillerymen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery are 'the Gunners'; its divisional commander is the CRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: One contended with a climber hanging on

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vied means competed or contended

explanation.surface: A mountaineer struggled while a fellow climber dangled from the rope.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'climber' is not a mountaineer but a plant, ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered with a creeping plant like ivy clinging to the walls.

clue.text: Exponent of banned books

definitions.meaning: in algebra the power to which a number is raised
the Roman Catholic Church's list of forbidden reading

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a mathematical power and the Church's catalogue of prohibited works.

clue.text: Homely music of a Gregorian chant

parts.note: homely means plain, unadorned
a song is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Simple music sung in Gregorian style.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied single-line medieval church singing, of which Gregorian is the best-known kind.

clue.text: Kept behind. bars at Oxbridge

parts.note: an undergraduate confined to college after the gates are shut as a punishment

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a student punished by being confined to college is said to be gated: kept behind the college gates. Oxbridge means Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Confined within college as a disciplinary measure, behind locked gates.

clue.text: Strangely uneven quality?

parts.note: both strangeness and the property of a number not divisible by two

explanation.definitionFit: It means peculiarity, and also the property of numbers like 3 and 7 that cannot be halved evenly.

clue.text: Complaint in metal, maybe :

indicators.note: maybe says the letters given could form something else, a cue to rearrange them

explanation.surface: An illness that might be found in metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' signals rearranging IN METAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is a minor illness or disorder.

clue.text: It may be hailed as the original fiscal measure

definitions.text: It may be hailed as the original fiscal measure

parts.words: It may be hailed as the original fiscal measure
parts.note: a cab is hailed in the street; read as the first levy, tax number one, it gives tax plus the numeral I

explanation.walkthrough: You hail a cab; the word also splits as a tax followed by I, the Roman one, the 'original' or first.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car with a meter, flagged down in the street.

clue.text: Trade dives in ruins, because one hasn't this?

definitions.text: Trade dives in ruins, because one hasn't this?

indicators.note: letters in ruins have been wrecked and must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A business collapses because nobody promoted it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: TRADE DIVES rearranged, and the reason a business fails, it was never publicised.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that has not promoted itself publicly may see its trade collapse.
